results.screen:
Tam's hand leaves the gunwale and finds the folded paper by touch, the way it found your coins. His thumb moves over the seal, slowly, and his milk-white eyes stay fixed on nothing at all. He turns the letter over, then back again, and sets it flat against his knee.

"I can't read it," he says. "The river fever took my eyes, and I can't make out a word of anything now. Whatever's written there, you'll have to tell me yourself, or have Mira tell me."

The pole dips and the ferry leans into the current. Up the bank Mira's lantern wobbles, unlit, and ahead the far shore is a dark line, nearer than it was. Tam holds the letter out toward you, waiting to hear what you'll do with it.

results.screen:
You put the ask to Morga and wait. She lays the spoon across the rim of the pot and wipes her burn-scarred hand on her apron, studying you the way a healer studies a splinter before she draws it. Then the stiffness goes out of her shoulders. "Aye, that I can allow, my duck. Sit where they can see you and hear you, and keep your questions in your pocket until they ask for them." Her gaze drops to the low stool by the door, then lifts back to your face, and she gives a short nod, as though the matter is settled between you. On the stove the kettle lifts toward its rattle, and Morga waits with her hand still resting on the scrubbed table, watching to see where you will settle yourself.
